summary: The paper proposes a constraint-based method in which a compiler records, for each parallelizable loop, constraints on array distributions weighted by estimated execution-time penalties, then combines them into one distribution per array. It demonstrates the method by hand on five Fortran programs and measures one of them, tred2, on a 16-processor iPSC/2.
why_read: It is an early and clearly argued account of choosing array distributions by weighing constraints, and it shows why component alignment and processor-grid shape matter.
main_contribution: A constraint-based strategy for choosing alignment, sequentialization, block-cyclic parameters, processor-grid shape and replication for whole regular programs.
main_limitation: The authors state that the strategy is not guaranteed optimal because the problem is NP-hard, and that its quality measures rest on compile-time assumptions about loop bounds and branch probabilities.
evaluation_method: Hand simulation of the strategy on five programs, with measured execution times for one program (tred2) on a 16-processor iPSC/2 hypercube
